# capybara v0.7.0

This release adds local capture, investigation, and evaluation workflows to the CLI, TUI, and Web view.

## New in this release

- Send traces to a running TUI through OTLP or loopback HTTP JSON events. `capybara listen` runs the same receiver and analyzer without the TUI; `capybara sample` loads a labelled first trace.
- The TUI Connect screen shows the bound endpoint and copyable integration snippets. Command search and responsive panes make the trace, cost, context, and resource views easier to reach.
- The Web workspace now includes Overview, Explore, Trace, Datasets, Prompts, and Usage. The optional hub adds project tokens, editor actions, backup, retention, and webhook alerts on one machine.
- Linked logs, incident groups and evidence packets, cost provenance, datasets, scenario runs, scores, and paired experiments support investigation and regression checks.
- Existing demos are collected in the README, including a pinned public Agents SDK failure. The Web screenshots come from the browser check's labelled synthetic run.

## Fixes

- Avoid a false `malformed_arguments` finding when LangGraph records Python dictionary text as `text/plain`.
- Reject incomplete provider usage when enforcing the optional proxy's soft budget.
- Require patched Python telemetry dependencies and correct Node SDK error spans.

## Install

Use the binaries attached to this release, or run:

```sh
go install github.com/tonquoc0407/capybara/cmd/capybara@v0.7.0
```

See the [README](https://github.com/tonquoc0407/capybara#readme) for the TUI and Web tour, and the [full changes](https://github.com/tonquoc0407/capybara/compare/v0.6.0...v0.7.0) for the commit history.

The local JSON event receiver accepts same-machine clients only and has no API key. The hub uses SQLite on one machine and binds localhost by default. The proxy budget is a soft session limit; it is not a provider invoice or a persistent spending cap.
